newsitem.title: FRANCE: Publicis chief denies discord over stake sale plan.
newsitem.headline: Publicis chief denies discord over stake sale plan.

text.p: Maurice Levy, chairman of French advertising group Publicis, denied there was any conflict between two daughters of the late founder of Publicis, Marcel Bleustein-Blanchet, over one daughter's plan to sell her Publicis holdings.
He told Reuters late on Monday that one daughter, Michele Bleustein-Blanchet, had no timescale for selling all or part of the 20 percent she held directly or indirectly in Publicis.

Levy was reacting to a report in Monday's edition of the financial daily La Tribune that said Michele Bleustein-Blanchet's plans were being blocked by her sister, Elisabeth Badinter, who chairs the Publicis holding company Somarel. Publicis is one of Europe's biggest advertising agency networks, with offices in nearly 20 countries.

"Michele Bleustein-Blanchet and Elisabeth Badinter both want the group to remain independant and to be controlled by the family," Levy said in a telephone interview. There was no question of any conflict or any quarrel between them, he added.
Michele Bleustein-Blanchet may ultimately seek to sell the seven percent she holds directly in Publicis on the market, Levy said.
"Michele Bleustein-Blanchet is fully in agreement with the group's strategy and its international development and has backed all the Publicis board's decisions," he said.
"Control of the group remain in the hands of family shareholders and is broad enough to envisage opening Publicis to outsiders," he said.
However Levy said there were currently no talks with anyone interested in becoming a Publicis shareholder.
Members of the family of Marcel Bleustein, who died a year ago, own 60 percent of Publicis.
Michele Bleustein-Blanchet owns a third of holding company Somarel, as does Elisabeth Badinter.
Somarel owns 38.4 percent of Publicis's capital and 45 percent of its voting rights.
